written.action: Rotate administrator and VPN credentials, especially on FortiGate appliances, and enforce multi-factor sign-in on all remote access. Audit for administrator accounts you did not create and patch edge devices quickly.
written.exec: Ransomware on industrial firms keeps rising and manufacturing bears most of it; remote access and edge devices are the common entry.
written.plain: Security firm Dragos counted 1,266 ransomware attacks on factories and other industrial companies in three months, 11% more than the previous quarter. Most began through remote-access equipment or stolen VPN passwords.

key_findings: Dragos tracked 1,266 ransomware incidents affecting industrial organisations in Q3 2026, up 11% from 1,140 in Q2.
Manufacturing accounted for 876 incidents (69%); North America had 566, of which 473 were in the United States.
Qilin claimed 195 victims and The Gentlemen 167; distinct ransomware brands hitting industry rose from 70 to 99.
Entry came through internet-facing edge devices and enterprise applications, often within days of disclosure, and stolen VPN credentials.
Cl0p returned with 35 victims via PTC Windchill and FlexPLM exploitation; no operator was seen manipulating a control system directly.
recommendations: Rotate administrator and VPN credentials, especially on FortiGate appliances.
Enforce MFA on all remote access.
Audit for administrator accounts you did not create.
Patch edge devices and enterprise applications rapidly and run continuous external attack surface management.
Enforce strict policies for remote monitoring and management tools.

recommendations: Apply Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update or the OpenJDK fixed releases, internet-facing systems first.

written.title: Unit 42 describes Com-affiliated vishing campaigns stealing data from financial, healthcare and legal firms
written.date_note: Date of Unit 42's report; the activity it describes runs since August 2026.

key_findings: Com-affiliated actors are running repeated vishing-led data theft and extortion waves against financial services, healthcare and legal organizations, mainly in the U.S., UK and Australia.

Callers pose as IT support and send employees to tailored adversary-in-the-middle phishing pages that capture credentials and MFA approvals, after which the attackers enroll their own MFA devices within minutes.
A newly described cluster, CL-CRI-1264, mainly targets healthcare and pharma and has used personal mobile devices as well as corporate workstations.
A malicious Chrome-impersonating browser extension, sideloaded in Developer Mode, adds keylogging, cookie theft and a DevTools-based remote control module.
Australian targeting rose from under 1% of observed subdomains in August and September to about 13% in October, making it the second most-targeted country.
recommendations: Tighten help desk identity verification.
Move to phishing-resistant MFA such as FIDO2 or passkeys.
Use allowlists for browser extensions.
Gain visibility into identity actions.
Alert on unauthorized data exports.

The post names no victim organisations or countries.
recommendations: Apply the Broadcom patch immediately.
Use the Mandiant VCSA Hardening and Logging Tool after testing and change control.
Hunt with the YARA rules and indicators in the GTI collection.

validation.note: The CERT-In advisory page was read in full; Telangana Today (IANS) reports the same advisory. The Hacker News (23 November) adds the I4C advisory on banks, NBFCs and fintechs; the I4C PDF itself would not load (connection reset).

key_findings: Attackers alter business records or approval relationships, then push transactions through legitimate payment processes; payment APIs are not the only target.
Affected parties now include technology service providers for government-linked payment processes and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts, as well as banks and financial institutions.
Transactions can pass normal application and approval checks even though the underlying records were changed without authorisation.
CERT-In's threat hunting found AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks used against enterprises, service providers, government bodies and academic and research institutions.
These frameworks automate reconnaissance, credential attacks and parallel intrusion tasks by multiple agents, and adapt attack steps when blocked.
recommendations: Limit which provider systems can change payment records or approve transactions, and reconcile payment instructions against independent records.
Require independent verification for high-risk payment changes and agree log access and suspension procedures with providers.
Technology and payout providers should separate client environments, restrict admin and control-plane privileges, and monitor record changes alongside privileged activity and approvals.

Review internet-facing applications, identities, privileged and service accounts and external connections, and check logs for reconnaissance, credential use, admin activity and outbound data transfers.
Report incidents to CERT-In within six hours and unauthorised financial transactions at cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930.

The Hacker News reported on 23 November that a separate I4C advisory says such attacks on banks, NBFCs and fintechs led to multi-crore unauthorised transactions.

written.title: CISA adds SAP NetWeaver flaw CVE-2025-42884 to its known-exploited catalog
written.date_note: Date of CISA's alert; it gives no earlier day for the first exploitation.
written.summary: CISA's alert of 20 November lists SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-42884 among four vulnerabilities added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. Heise reports the flaw is a JNDI injection in NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, rated CVSS 6.5, that SAP fixed in its November 2025 Patchday.
written.plain: US agency CISA says a flaw in SAP NetWeaver is being exploited in attacks. Heise says SAP released a fix in November 2025.
written.exec: CISA lists the SAP NetWeaver flaw as actively exploited, so unpatched systems are exposed.
written.action: General advice: confirm SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal has the fix SAP released in its November 2025 Patchday.

written.title: ExaTrack: Vmcloudoor Linux backdoor poses as cloud agents on Alibaba, Tencent and Huawei VMs
written.date_note: Date of ExaTrack's publication; the page gives no earlier discovery date.
written.org: Linux virtual machines on Chinese cloud platforms
written.summary: ExaTrack reported on 19 November a Linux backdoor it calls Vmcloudoor, found during a hunting session, that disguises itself as a host agent on cloud virtual machines. According to ExaTrack, it renames its process to match the cloud provider's agents and takes commands through Alibaba OSS storage; the targeted environments are Alibaba (mainly), Tencent and Huawei. ExaTrack assumes the author is a Chinese pentester, potentially running red team engagements.
written.plain: Researchers at ExaTrack found hidden remote-control software for Linux servers on Alibaba, Tencent and Huawei clouds that pretends to be the cloud provider's own helper program, so administrators are less likely to notice it.
written.exec: A backdoor that hides as the cloud provider's own agent targets Linux servers on Alibaba, Tencent and Huawei clouds, ExaTrack reports.
written.action: General advice: on Alibaba, Tencent and Huawei cloud servers, check processes that carry cloud agent names, and hunt with the indicators and YARA rule ExaTrack published with its report.

key_findings: Vmcloudoor is a Linux x64 implant found during a hunting session; ExaTrack obtained only its helper module.
It checks for cloud agent paths and processes and renames itself to match one, blending in with the processes of the targeted cloud environment.
Command and control runs through Alibaba OSS; the targeted environments are Alibaba (mainly), Tencent and Huawei.
ExaTrack assumes the author is a Chinese pentester, potentially running dedicated red team engagements.

validation.note: Single origin: ExaTrack, the firm that found the implant (exatrack.com, 19 Nov, read). GBHackers (23 Nov, read) only relays ExaTrack and is not independent. ExaTrack names no victims.
